one_line: Satavahana matriarch and donor who dedicated the famed Nashik cave inscription to her son Gautamiputra and grandson Pulumavi.

appearance.age_look: Late 50s to early 60s, medium height, dignified posture with a sturdy, matronly build reflecting age and status.
appearance.face: Oval face with soft jawline, warm medium-brown complexion, fine smile lines around the eyes and mouth, straight nose, gently arched brows; default expression calm and composed with a subtle, knowing half-smile that suggests quiet authority.
appearance.hair: Dark brown-black hair oiled and neatly parted in the middle, drawn back into a low, tight bun at the nape wrapped in a thin off-white cloth band, with a simple gold circular forehead ornament (tilaka-like disc) pinned at the hairline and no crown.
appearance.costume: A region-accurate early Satavahana-era sari: unstitched cloth in muted deep red with a narrow mustard-yellow border, wrapped in an early draped style with the lower garment tightly wound to the ankles and pleated in front, the upper end (pallu) brought around the torso and over the left shoulder to modestly cover the upper body; beneath, a simple short-sleeved blouse suggested only by darker red edges; bare midriff is NOT visible, the drape kept high and secure; jewellery consists of medium-thick plain gold bangles on both wrists, a single gold torque-like necklace close to the neck, small round gold ear studs, and a thin waist cord visible as a slight line under the sari; she is barefoot, as appropriate for a cave-donation context, with the sari’s hem just above the ground and a subtle woven texture indicating cotton.
appearance.signature: A rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a thin cord, held carefully in her left hand as a symbol of the inscription she commissioned and her role as donor and eulogist.

ref_desc: Gautami Balashri is a warm medium-brown, late-middle-aged woman with an oval face and calm half-smile, dark hair in a low bun wrapped with a cloth band and a small gold forehead disc, wearing a deep-red mustard-bordered Satavahana-style sari draped modestly over a blouse with simple gold jewellery and bare feet, always holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript, in a palette of deep red, mustard yellow, off-white, warm brown and dull gold.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Gautami Balashri, a dignified Satavahana matriarch, late 50s, medium height and sturdy build, with an oval face, warm medium-brown complexion, fine smile lines and a calm, knowing half-smile, straight nose and gently arched brows; her dark brown-black hair is oiled, center-parted and pulled into a low tight bun at the nape wrapped with a thin off-white cloth band, with a single small round gold disc ornament centered at the hairline, no crown or elaborate headdress. She wears a historically plausible early Satavahana regional sari made of cotton: a deep-red unstitched cloth with a narrow mustard-yellow border, wrapped tightly to the ankles with front pleats and the upper end brought around the torso and over the left shoulder so that her upper body is fully and modestly covered, with the drape kept high enough that no midriff is exposed; subtly indicate a simple matching darker-red short-sleeved blouse only by the edges at the sleeves and neckline beneath the drape. Add modest jewellery: a plain gold torque-like necklace close to the neck, small round gold ear studs, medium-thick plain gold bangles on both wrists, and a faint line of a thin waist cord visible under the sari folds; keep her barefoot as appropriate for a cave-donation setting, with the sari hem nearly touching the ground and showing a light woven texture. In her left hand she always holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with a cord as her signature prop, while her right hand rests relaxed at her side or lightly touches the sari drape. Use a restrained palette of deep red, mustard yellow, off-white, warm medium-brown skin tones and dull gold accents, and present front, side and three-quarter views to emphasize the consistent hairstyle, modest sari drape, jewellery and the ever-present manuscript prop.
